correctness.rationale: The stationary 3-dimensional linear Gaussian drift eigenvalues are -a,-d,-b with all positive. Independent observer noises have zero cross-spectrum. Exact cross-spectrum subtraction gives delta(t)=2D_f*c1*c2*(d-a)*F(t) with F(t)=(2/pi) int_0^infty omega*sin(omega*t)/[(omega²+a²)(omega²+d²)(omega²+b²)] d omega and Fprime(0)=1/[(a+d)(a+b)(d+b)]. Writing each Laplace Green kernel ell_r(t)=exp(-r|t|)/(2r) and G=ell_a*ell_d*ell_b yields F=-2Gprime>0 for every t>0 by strict monotonicity of convolution of positive symmetric decreasing kernels. Distinct poles give a three-term sum of exponentials and equal poles give confluent polynomial-exponential terms. Its derivative lies in a Chebyshev space of total order 3, so at most two real zeros including multiplicity; Fprime(0)>0 and its positive decaying eventual tail forces exactly one positive simple maximum (any tangent would violate the zero bound). Gaussian reversibility for observed two-probe covariance is equivalent to a=d when c1*c2 !=0. Triple equal rates κ give F=e^{-κt}(κt)(1+κt)/(8κ⁴); differentiation yields 1+z-z², hence unique optimum at κt=(1+sqrt5)/2. Smooth positive-rate perturbation and simple root yield coalescence. Independent symbolic differentiation and sampled positive-rate checks corroborate; full universal statement follows from Chebyshev/convolution proof.
